t.3.55.2: As he hurried on, eager to see Maithilī, a jackal with a harsh cry then howled behind him.
t.3.55.1: Having slain Mārīca, the rākṣasa who could change his form at will and was roaming in the guise of a deer, Rāma swiftly turned back along the path.
t.3.55.3: Perceiving its cry, dreadful and hair-raising, he grew anxious at the voice of the jackal and fell to brooding.
t.3.55.4: Alas, I think it an evil omen, the way this jackal howls. May all be well with Vaidehī, and may she not be devoured by the rākṣasas!
t.3.55.6: Hearing that cry, Saumitri will then leave Maithilī and, sent by her alone, will swiftly come here to my side.
t.3.55.5: But if Lakṣmaṇa should hear the cry raised by Mārīca in the form of a deer, Mārīca having discerned and closely marked my voice...
t.3.55.7: Surely the rākṣasas, acting together, sought the slaying of Sītā; and one of them, having become a golden deer, drew me away from the hermitage.
t.3.55.8: Having lured him far away, the rākṣasa Mārīca was struck down by an arrow, and he cried out the words, 'Alas, Lakṣmaṇa, I am slain!'
t.3.55.9: Will it be well with the two of them, left without me in the forest? For on account of Janasthāna I have made enemies of the rākṣasas, and many terrible omens are seen today.
t.3.55.10: Brooding thus, having heard the howl of the jackal and thinking of how he himself had been lured away by the rākṣasa in the form of a deer, Rāma, the Rāghava, came to Janasthāna, filled with apprehension.
t.3.55.12: Having seen those exceedingly dreadful omens, Rāghava then saw Lakṣmaṇa approaching, his radiance gone.
t.3.55.11: Beasts and birds came up to that great-souled one, wretched and dejected in mind, keeping him on their left, and they uttered dreadful cries.
t.3.55.13: Then, not far off, that Lakṣmaṇa met with Rāma, he dejected with the dejected one, sorrowful with him who shared in sorrow.
t.3.55.14: Then his elder brother sharply rebuked Lakṣmaṇa, who had come to him after leaving Sītā alone in the desolate forest frequented by rākṣasas.
t.3.55.15: Taking hold of his left hand, the delight of the Raghus spoke to Lakṣmaṇa these harsh words, sweet in their outcome, like one in deep distress.
t.3.55.17: I have no doubt at all, O hero, that the daughter of Janaka has perished, or else has been devoured by the rākṣasas who roam the forest.
t.3.55.16: Ah, Lakṣmaṇa, you have done a blameworthy thing in leaving Sītā and coming here, gentle one. Will any good come of it at all?
t.3.55.18: Since inauspicious omens are appearing to me in such great abundance, O Lakṣmaṇa, shall we indeed find Sītā safe and whole?
t.3.55.19: For this demon, looking like a deer, lured me on as I followed it far away, and it was killed somehow, with great effort; only as it was dying did it become a rākṣasa again.
t.3.55.20: My mind here is dejected and joyless, and my left eye is twitching. Without doubt, Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā is not there: she has been carried off, or she is dead, or she is wandering somewhere on the path.
